name: Aging and Disability Resources for Colorado (ADRC)
organization: Colorado Department of Human Services, State Unit on Aging
description: A statewide line that connects you to your local Area Agency on Aging for meals, in-home services, transportation, caregiver support and senior legal assistance. Military service is not required.
next_step: Call 844-265-2372 (1-844-COL-ADRC) from anywhere in Colorado. Choose a county above for the direct number of its Area Agency on Aging.
constraints: Each program has its own eligibility and waitlist.

name: Colorado Long-Term Care Ombudsman Program
organization: Colorado State Long-Term Care Ombudsman Program
description: Statewide advocacy for residents of long-term care facilities, delivered through 16 regional ombudsman programs.
next_step: Choose your county for its regional ombudsman, or call the state ombudsman at 303-862-3524. To report mistreatment of an at-risk adult, call the Adult Protective Services intake number at the county department of human services where the adult lives. For immediate danger, call 911.
constraints: The ombudsman acts with the resident’s permission and is not a licensing or enforcement agency.

source_evidence.title: Colorado State Library: Colorado Long-Term Care Ombudsman Program annual report (federal fiscal year 2022)
source_evidence.scope: State ombudsman phone and the 16 regional programs; search excerpt.

source_evidence.title: Colorado Department of Human Services: report mistreatment or self-neglect of an at-risk adult
source_evidence.scope: Reports go to the county Adult Protective Services intake number; the page gives no statewide reporting number.

name: Colorado Legal Services
description: Free civil legal help for people with low income and for older adults (60 and older), including help responding to an eviction notice. Not criminal or traffic law.
next_step: Apply at coloradolegalservices.org or call the main office. Have your county and the legal problem ready.
constraints: Applicants are screened; this is not a quick-advice hotline. Income, case type and capacity limits apply, and local offices serve different counties.

source_evidence.title: Colorado state publication: free or low-cost legal services (April 2024)
source_evidence.scope: Main office phone; search excerpt.

source_evidence.title: Larimer County Senior Access Points: Colorado Legal Services
source_evidence.scope: Senior Law Project for people 60 and older, with screening before help; search excerpt.

name: VA medical centers serving Colorado
description: VA Eastern Colorado Health Care System: Rocky Mountain Regional VA Medical Center, Aurora (303-399-8020), with community clinics across eastern Colorado, including Colorado Springs, La Junta, Lamar and Salida. VA Western Colorado Health Care System: Grand Junction VA Medical Center (970-242-0731).
next_step: Use VA’s facility locator with your ZIP code to find the closest clinic and its medical center. Not enrolled yet? Ask your County Veterans Service Officer for help applying.
constraints: VA does not publish county lists for these systems, so this card does not assign counties. Your VA care team may be at a different clinic or system; follow what VA tells you.

name: Rocky Mountain Human Services: veteran housing help (SSVF)
description: VA-funded Supportive Services for Veteran Families (SSVF, grant 20-CO-020): case management, help keeping a home, rapid rehousing and short-term financial help for low-income veteran households.
next_step: Call SSVF intake with your county and housing situation: whether you are homeless now or at risk of losing housing, and who lives with you. A second intake number is listed: 719-323-2600.
constraints: Serves only the areas listed; check that yours is included. Veteran-household, income and housing-status screening applies.
County and intake details come from VA’s FY26 SSVF provider intake list; confirm current service when calling.
